approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local edits, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity checks admit a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted archive uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto covariance to predict that pool. It currently fills the evaluation batch with independent correlated posterior draws, removing each chosen identity before the next draw. Accepted scores update both the breeding population and prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make later batch choices account for uncertainty already represented by earlier pending selections. After choosing a molecule, condition the remaining draw residuals on that molecule taking its current posterior mean. This reduces shared random excursions without changing the fitted model or its predicted means. Earlier siblings changed breeding state, molecular edits, fingerprint representation or fitted noise; none coordinated the pending choices through this within-batch conditioning. The test asks whether that coordination improves the use of the existing pool, with changed selections and conditional variance measured separately from score.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 completes all supplied replicas with macro mean 0.574343936523512 and population SD 0.012316775530180069. Its count-sensitive posterior is informative on the selected stream: chronological MSE is 0.0112691820515 versus the archive-mean baseline 0.0425042191038. Yet only 624 of 4350 evaluated offspring strictly beat their best generating parent, and 3529 lose. The targeted behavior is narrower than general predictive error: every batch position uses an independent draw from the same pre-batch joint distribution, and earlier choices only remove their exact indices. Later draws do not reduce uncertainty shared with already selected, still-unobserved molecules. A passive reconstruction of all 435 actual Parent pools with its earlier accepted archives, recorded normals and RDKit 2023.09.6 reproduces means within 9.68e-14 and function draws within 5.69e-14. Under noiseless conditioning at the earlier selections' current posterior means, the 3915 later Parent choices have mean explainable sampling-variance fraction 0.0419994, median 0.00835923, 95th percentile 0.199977 and maximum 0.929065. Thus typical redundancy is modest, with a material tail. Applying only the proposed residual projection on these logged inputs preserves all 435 first choices, changes 660 of 4350 positions and 302 of 435 batch sets, and retains 3866 original set memberships. Mean absolute pairwise posterior correlation changes from 0.0489841 to 0.0457580; only 174 batches decrease it. These are unlabeled decision counterfactuals, not score estimates or proof that lower correlation is useful. The older selector evidence at n-fc2c108a5253 likewise confirms uncertainty-dependent choices without isolating their score contribution. The Parent's 76.9 percent nominal latent-interval coverage also cautions that model-implied redundancy need not match real score dependence.
hypothesis: Condition later within-batch posterior draw residuals on earlier selected pool molecules taking their current posterior means, so pending selections remove shared sampling uncertainty before subsequent masked maximization.

finding_summary.headline: Conditioning changes 287 batches, but the mean score falls slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes a real allocation effect and narrows its value: removing some shared posterior variation is insufficient by itself to improve the final best score on this panel. The intervention reaches a modest typical redundancy opportunity, with a larger tail, and still permits related high-mean molecules to occupy the same batch. Even on identical pools, average count-fingerprint similarity increased slightly while posterior correlation decreased. Lower model correlation therefore cannot substitute for chemical diversity or score evidence. More parent-beating offspring and more incremental incumbent improvements also proved insufficient as proxies for the final endpoint.

The lower MSE describes a changed adaptive search stream; the fitted prediction model and its means remained unchanged on shared inputs. Mean conditioning supplied no new labels and did not repair the already poor uncertainty coverage. Whether real pending outcomes would support these zero-innovation constraints remains open, and unobserved counterfactual choices cannot answer it. The molecular assessment further limits the small core-coverage gain: smaller assemblies now contain many more small or tightly bridged rings, while reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Graph-core novelty is not evidence of feasible chemistry. A stronger test of useful batch coordination would need to connect model redundancy to actual score dependence or chemically meaningful alternatives; this run rules out treating the measured contraction alone as evidence of that connection.
finding_summary.results:
All 3,915 within-batch projections executed correctly. On identical Child pools and random draws, they preserved all 435 first choices but changed 600 of 4,350 selection positions and 287 of 435 batch sets. Later selected molecules lost an average 3.30% of their original sampling variance; the median reduction was 0.81%. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation fell from 0.04721 to 0.04571, and mean nonempty molecular-core coverage rose slightly from 7.06 to 7.14 cores per ten-molecule batch. Neither consequence was universal. All batches and evaluations completed.

The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.57434 to 0.57250, a change of -0.00184 against the registered +0.002 minimum. One seed improved and two declined. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.01151 and zaleplon by 0.00714, while DRD2 fell by 0.01705, median similarity by 0.00706 and decoration hopping by 0.00376. Strict improvements over the best generating parent increased from 624 to 677 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 278. On their respective scored streams, prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.009821, but mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.534 and nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 76.9% to 76.1%. Correct conditioning and better local improvement counts did not deliver the intended final-score gain.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families retain reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry; smaller assemblies now carry many more small rings.
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-521f362b3777 produces substantial organic molecules with aromatic and saturated heterocycles, carbonyls, tertiary amines and frequent halogens, together with a small tail of molecular fragments. All five supplied objectives have trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Each task contains 900 recorded evaluations, including 870 optimizer proposals across the supplied seeds. Digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9609 to 0.9839 and aromatic-SMILES rates from 0.8667 to 0.9759; these are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Explicit charge and stereocentre string rates are zero throughout. Ring systems and aromatic chemistry are rich, synthetic plausibility is questionable, and drug-likeness is moderate because ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with reactive functionalities and implausible topologies. Structural diversity is moderate: numerous core identities coexist with strong concentration around individual high-scoring families.

A passive RDKit 2023.09.6 reading of every supplied Child and Parent trajectory finds all 4,350 optimizer occurrences in each corpus parseable. Child molecules have median heavy-atom counts of 25, 38, 32, 33 and 27 in the fixed task order. Compared with Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, occurrences above 50 heavy atoms fall from 313 to 100, while occurrences with a perceived three- or four-membered ring rise from 268 to 1,372. Small rings alone do not establish a liability; the concerning examples include a ring-embedded alkyne, highly bridged aromatic graphs and substituted aziridines. RDKit identifies unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2,631 Child proposals versus 2,284 Parent proposals, with no explicitly assigned centres in either. The output therefore explores substantial three-dimensional connectivity without specifying stereoisomers. Neutral SMILES also contain many potentially basic amines; zero formal charge must not be read as absence of ionizable nitrogen.

Observed scores below are the supplied scores, and comparisons describe associated chemistry without assigning mechanism activation, biological activity, synthetic accessibility or a new quality score. No particular missing target pharmacophore can be identified solely from these trajectories. Full passive counts, motif definitions, descriptor calculations and path/seed/evaluation references are recorded in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-01-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json; its companion .audit.py reproduces the audit. Aggregate chemical counts include optimizer occurrences, and perceived ring/core counts do not establish distinct feasible synthetic scaffolds.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are mostly compact aromatic heterocycles: median 25 heavy atoms, ring-closure rate 0.9678 and aromatic-SMILES rate 0.9655. The best cited family is a dimethylphenyl-substituted, partially saturated N-N heterocycle with a hydroxyl on the imine carbon and an N-acyl/thiocarbonyl connection to pyridine. Its leading member has 24 heavy atoms, a five-membered N-N ring and two aromatic six-membered rings. A second leading family has a fused nitrogen-rich aromatic system, methoxy/vinyl substitution and a ketone-methylene-pyridine arm; its cited member also has 24 heavy atoms. These families have recognizable aromatic/carbonyl organization, but the sulfur-rich connections are less conventional than ordinary amides. Parent high-score molecules were predominantly compact indole-like/carbonyl families, often with N-halogen or N-S substituents. Child and Parent both have a median of 25 heavy atoms, while thiocarbonyl-containing proposals rise from 19 to 212 out of 870.
liabilities: The leading N-N family contains a thiocarbonyl next to a carbonyl; some descendants repeat the thiocarbonyl. These are potentially reactive, tautomer-sensitive connections whose preparation and stability are not established by the scores.

The full stream contains 223 N-halogen-bearing proposals out of 870, although the highest 30 scored proposals contain none. Halogen attachment to heteroatoms is a persistent exploration product rather than an essential feature of the leading cited families.
The high-score examples retain either undefined stereochemistry or substantial aromatic planarity; low-score fragments show loss of the useful molecular framework.
missing_features: The high-score set supplies few independent, chemically conventional alternatives to the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. Its repeated nitrogen-position isomers give tied scores, so the observed headroom cannot be assigned to a particular missing aza position.
The partially saturated N-N family has unspecified stereochemistry. Stereo-defined realizations and explicit tautomer alternatives are not demonstrated; their score contribution is unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole aryl carboxamide scores 0.3051048084; the hydroxylated N-N/thiocarbonyl family reaches 0.4823613572 and the fused aza-aromatic ketone family reaches 0.4692371322. Molecular fragments such as the cited F and NBr score zero. Within the leading N-N family, adding a second adjacent thiocarbonyl coincides with 0.4712711079, below the shorter connection. The two cited pyridine nitrogen-position isomers both score 0.4823613572, and the corresponding nitrogen-position pair in the fused family both score 0.4692371322. Rearranging the fused family to the larger, partly saturated ring system in the cited seed-2 final molecule yields 0.1779108959. This supports a bounded aromatic/heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement over fragmentation or arbitrary ring remodeling; it does not demonstrate a unique rewarded nitrogen position. Parent seed-1 and seed-2 maxima are 0.4423126980 and 0.4484138510, alongside the different Child families just described; seed-0 instead has a lower Child maximum, 0.4182215872 versus 0.4576604702.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most extended proposal stream: median 38 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 71.7 and maximum length 232. Ring-closure and aromatic-SMILES rates are 0.9713 and 0.9690. The leading cited family joins two fused aza-aromatic ring systems and carries a cyclic carbonyl, nitrile/cyanate functionality, vinyl or alkynyl groups and fluorinated substituents. The highest molecule has 37 heavy atoms, four perceived aromatic rings, no hydrogen-bond donor and nine acceptors. The other seeds include peroxide-decorated nitrogen-rich carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich heteroaromatic assemblies with long unsaturated imine arms. These are recognizable functional groups assembled into increasingly demanding targets. Relative to Parent, median size falls from 41 to 38 heavy atoms and median perceived ring count from five to four; the high-score families still vary strongly by seed.
liabilities: Cyanate esters and the cited cumulated unsaturated nitrogen-containing arm add reactive or unusual chemistry to an already acceptor-rich aromatic family. The cyanate-bearing highest structures have no hydrogen-bond donors; their solubility is unmeasured.

The cited four-membered ring containing a triple bond is a severe geometric plausibility concern even though its SMILES parses. The repeated final assembly additionally combines multiple thiocarbonyls, a thioacyl chloride and an S-Cl group.
Peroxide-bearing proposals occur 188 times out of 870. The stream also retains large assemblies up to 116 heavy atoms, so reduced typical size has not removed growth extremes.
missing_features: Independent high-scoring core arrangements are poorly represented: 26 of the highest 30 scored proposals share the same nonempty Murcko core. The score-supported aza-aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is mostly revisited through side-chain decoration.

Comparable demonstrations of conventional, chemically robust substituents replacing the leading cyanate/unsaturated decorations are sparse. The trajectory establishes the scored arrangement, but does not show which simpler replacement would preserve that score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic fused dione scores 0.5483814828, versus 0.6264431006 for the leading linked aza-aromatic/cyanate family. The cited tiny fragments and cyclobutyne derivative all score 0.5. Several side-chain changes preserve exactly 0.6252529482 despite different carbon counts and substitution, consistent with a broad local plateau around the retained ring/polar-group pattern. Large size alone is not rewarded: the cited final repeated sulfur-rich assembly has 77 heavy atoms and score 0.5881847584, below the leading 37-heavy-atom molecule. The Child seed-1 maximum of 0.6264431006 accompanies a different four-ring aza-aromatic arrangement from Parent's 0.6199818406 family; seed-0 and seed-2 maxima instead decline from 0.6092799189 to 0.6026851747 and from 0.6169921410 to 0.6058367091. These observations do not isolate a missing decoration from hidden objective information.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are relatively compact saturated amines attached to halogenated aromatic carbocycles. The strongest cited family combines an N-propylpyrrolidine with a fluorinated indane-like unit; some descendants add chlorinated aziridines or azetidines, amino groups or additional heterocyclic bridges. The simple cited member has 19 heavy atoms and one aromatic ring, while the highest member has 23 heavy atoms and an additional aziridine. These have recognizable potentially basic nitrogens and substantial saturated carbon content. Across the whole stream the median is 32 heavy atoms, aromatic-SMILES rate 0.9701 and halogen rate 0.9816; other seeds include more flexible aryl/amine chains with sulfur functionalities. Parent already produces aryl/aliphatic-amine families. The Child has 375 proposals with three- or four-membered rings versus nine in Parent, while both contain many potentially ionizable amines.
liabilities: Substituted aziridines, including a carbon bearing chlorine, add potential ring-opening/reactivity liabilities. Azetidines themselves are plausible medicinal motifs; their exact substitution and the additional bridges still require chemical scrutiny.

Later cited structures introduce N-S connections and densely bridged ring systems without specifying stereochemistry. The full trajectory has 851 proposals with unspecified tetrahedral centres out of 870.
A high recorded score is not a binding measurement or a demonstration of chemical stability; no such measurements accompany the supplied molecular records.
missing_features: Stereo-defined realizations of the favorable amine/carbobicycle arrangement are absent. RDKit finds five unspecified tetrahedral centres in the highest cited structure and two in the simpler near-equal-scoring structure.

Charged alternatives to the neutral amine encodings are not shown. Protonation-state coverage in emitted molecules is therefore absent, although evaluator preparation and any score benefit from explicit charges cannot be inferred.

No missing receptor-binding motif is established by these near-maximal examples. The practical missing evidence is feasible geometry and stereochemical identity for the already represented amine/aryl arrangements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited methyl aryl sulfonate scores 0.0002467587 and the carboxylic-acid/amide/sulfonamide example 0.0006269216. These lie far below the N-propylpyrrolidine/fluorinated carbobicycle family. The highest aziridine-bearing molecule scores 0.9999959963, but the simpler analogue without that extra small N-ring already scores 0.9999918570; an azetidine-bearing relative scores 0.9999909620. The observed gradient supports retained basic-amine/aromatic-hydrophobic organization without requiring the additional reactive small ring. Scores near the top are too similar to justify chemical claims about those decorations. Parent seed-2 reaches 0.9912887883 with a larger aryl/heterocycle/amine structure, while Child reaches the cited compact family; Parent seed-1 reaches 0.9964552366 whereas Child's different aryl/amine/aziridine family reaches 0.9390186236.

per_task.generated_character: This stream concentrates on polycyclic aromatic/lactam/tertiary-amine assemblies with a median of 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings. Ring-closure and aromatic-SMILES rates are 0.9839 and 0.9759, while halogen rate is only 0.1103. The highest cited molecule has a propylphenyl group, a large N-methylated amino-lactam ring and a tightly bridged aromatic/lactam fragment. Other high members use fused or spiro aryl/ether/lactam arrangements attached to aza-aromatics. The functional groups are broadly medicinal, but the ring closures make many actual structures difficult synthetic propositions. Parent also has aryl-linked cyclic urea/lactam/amine families at the same median heavy-atom count; its median perceived ring count is four and its small-ring occurrence count is 102, versus 384 in Child.
liabilities: The cited leading family bridges aromatic carbons through very short rings. Some descendants contain multiple small rings nested around the aromatic/lactam fragment; sanitization does not resolve their geometric strain.
Large amino-lactam rings and spiro/fused closures create demanding conformational and synthetic problems. All of the highest 30 scored proposals have unspecified tetrahedral centres.

Literal graph diversity is extensive, including 642 nonempty Murcko cores over the proposals, but many differences are ring-closure changes within related aryl/carbonyl/amine chemistry. That count is not evidence for 642 practical synthetic scaffolds.
missing_features: Simpler, geometrically credible arrangements preserving the useful aromatic/amine/lactam combination are poorly represented among the leading Child structures. Ring richness is already ample; the missing chemical capability is coherent control of linkage topology.

Defined stereoisomers and a demonstrated conformationally realizable arrangement of the bridged fragments are absent. The data do not identify a particular missing atom or reference-derived pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused aromatic dione scores 0.1678386595 and the initial indole carboxamide 0.1351979950. Tiny fragments such as the cited sulfur species and peroxide score zero. The leading propylphenyl/polycyclic amino-lactam reaches 0.2308286232, and its ethylphenyl counterpart scores 0.2229882439. Adding aryl fluorine to the propyl analogue yields 0.2200478417. The cited spiro/bridged heterocyclic member reaches 0.2240892853. Thus the visible gradient favors a retained combination of aromatic groups, cyclic nitrogen and carbonyls over isolated fragments; it does not reward halogen addition generally. More intricate Child ring chemistry does not accompany a higher matched-seed maximum: Parent/Child values are 0.2227060618/0.2201656340, 0.2432151565/0.2308286232 and 0.2303516197/0.2240892853. This describes the molecular/score association only.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of a fused nitrogen-rich bicyclic dione attached to a fluorinated cyclobutene, with fluoroalkyl N/carbon substituents and either an acyl fluoride or a methyl ketone. The best cited acyl fluoride has 28 heavy atoms, three perceived rings, five fluorines, four nitrogens and three oxygens. It has no hydrogen-bond donor and several unspecified stereocentres. The full stream has a median of 27 heavy atoms, aromatic-SMILES rate 0.8667 and halogen rate 0.8540. Other seeds retain fluorinated N-rich carbonyl systems with N-F/O-F bonds, aryl hydroxylamine groups or unsaturated small rings. Parent already shows the N-rich carbonyl/fluorination theme at the same median size. Child proposals with acyl halides rise from Parent's one to 36 and those with small rings from 91 to 416, while N-halogen proposals decline from 534 to 457.
liabilities: Acyl fluorides are reactive acylating functionalities. Their occurrence among the highest scores makes synthetic isolation and stability a separate question from the recorded objective value.
N-F and O-F bonds recur in the trajectory, including the cited final N-fluorinated dione. The substituted cyclobutenes and unsaturated N-small-rings add geometric and stereochemical complexity.

The leading acyl-fluoride pair has four and three unspecified tetrahedral centres respectively. No emitted molecule has explicit stereochemistry, and the leading donor-free diones do not themselves establish physicochemical or biological suitability.
missing_features: The leading fluorine/N/carbonyl balance has little coverage in independent ring geometries: 19 of the highest 30 scored proposals share one nonempty Murcko core. Chemically robust, stereo-defined alternatives retaining that balance are not demonstrated.

The less-reactive methyl-ketone counterpart is already present near the leading score, so acyl fluoride is not a necessary feature of the observed high-score region. What remains missing is systematic exploration of such conventional functional-group placement across distinct feasible cores.
The data do not establish any particular absent binding group. Absence of explicit protonation and stereochemical alternatives is observable, but their score contribution is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial nonfluorinated fused dione scores 0.0020944535. The highest cited acyl fluorides score 0.6603512652, and the methyl-ketone analogues score 0.6386273038. The cited fluorine-relocated pairs retain identical scores within each group. Passive atom counts show that the leading acyl fluoride and ketone share the same carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine inventories, despite different placement of fluorine and carbonyl functionality. Adding another fluorine in the cited acyl-fluoride family gives 0.6290826885, so indiscriminate fluorination is not a monotonic route upward. The overall worst initial large chlorinated ester scores 7.6850703896e-27; cited single-atom fragments are also extremely low. The trajectory supports a bounded size/heteroatom/fluorine balance, but does not isolate which objective components cause that balance. Parent seed-1's aryl/N-rich-dione family reaches 0.4870057306, while Child's cyclobutene family reaches 0.6603512652; seed-0 and seed-2 maxima instead change from 0.6510211907 to 0.5728430096 and 0.6025252355 to 0.5418815215.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimizer proposal parses in the matching RDKit, yet the digest contains a four-membered cyclic alkyne at 0.5, heavily bridged aromatic/lactam graphs, a cyanate-bearing aza-aromatic compound at 0.6264431006 and an acyl fluoride at 0.6603512652. Across the complete proposal set, small-ring occurrences rise from 268 in Parent to 1,372 in Child. The specific bonding arrangements, rather than the mere existence of small rings, motivate the concern.
transferable_gaps.gap: Candidate construction does not consistently preserve chemically credible bonding and ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Investigate generic chemically coherent bond and functional-group transformations, together with topology checks for the resulting graph. Preserve access to ordinary cyclic amines, ketones and amides while distinguishing specific strained or reactive products. Assess any restrictions against the generator's own accepted feedback; chemical plausibility is not guaranteed by a higher score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the linked aza-aromatic/cyanate high-score family, 26 of the highest 30 scored proposals share one nonempty Murcko core; in the fluorinated fused-dione family, 19 of 30 share one. The digest shows tied scores for several side-chain or nitrogen-position changes. Other streams generate many literal cores, including heavily bridged variants, so this is local family concentration rather than universal collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-score exploration often changes substituents within one core without supplying independent chemically coherent frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make alternative ring and linker organizations accessible while retaining favorable combinations of functional groups inferred from finite accepted feedback. Measure chemically interpretable scaffold changes separately from changes in terminal decoration or arbitrary extra ring closures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest explicit stereocentre rate is zero for every proposal stream. Passive perception finds unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2,631 of 4,350 Child proposals, including five in the highest cited amine/carbobicycle and four in a leading fluorinated dione. Parent also has no explicitly assigned centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereo-rich connectivity without specifying the resulting stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent stereochemical assignment and preservation when editing tetrahedral centres or closing rings, using stable isomeric identities within the existing interface. Determine usefulness from actual feedback; the present scores do not prove a benefit from enumerating stereoisomers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest charged_rate is zero, and the passive audit finds no charged Child or Parent proposal. Nevertheless the leading saturated-amine structures include tertiary pyrrolidine nitrogens, and multiple amino-lactam families contain potentially basic ring nitrogens. The neutral-only record is a representational gap, not evidence that basic centres are absent.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures provide no explicit charge-state alternatives for their ionizable functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the existing oracle and identity contracts permit it, investigate generic, chemically supported protonation and tautomer moves with consistent identity handling. Check how the evaluator prepares these states before assuming that explicitly emitting them would change outcomes; no hidden objective identity is needed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child contains 109 optimizer occurrences with at most five heavy atoms and 100 with more than 50, compared with 122 and 313 in Parent. Digest fragments receive zero or near-minimal scores in several streams. The cited repeated sulfur-rich assembly has 77 heavy atoms and score 0.5881847584, below the 37-heavy-atom aza-aromatic molecule at 0.6264431006. Reduced growth extremes have not eliminated fragmentation or oversized repeats.
transferable_gaps.gap: Mutations and recombinations still lose useful molecular scale or create excessive repeated assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve coherent functional-group and ring units during graph changes, and use the generator's own accepted size/structure feedback to explore productive growth or contraction. Any molecular-scale control should remain generic and adaptive; these trajectories do not justify a universal fixed target size.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
